title: Availability updates immediately when rent record is created
gherkin:
Feature: Immediate Availability Synchronization
  Scenario: Availability updates immediately when rent record is created
    Given an item is available for rent
    When an authorized user creates a new rent record for that item
    Then the item's availability status is updated immediately
    And the item is marked as unavailable for the rent period
rationale: Verifies that availability synchronization occurs in real time when a rent record is created, ensuring the system reflects the current lifecycle state immediately.
usedContextItems: Availability must be updated in real time when rent records are created, modified, cancelled, or completed|Availability status changes take effect immediately when triggered by authorized users

From: ops_lead@toolchain.com
To: dev_leads@toolchain.com, pm_team@toolchain.com
Date: 2026-02-20 14:00
Subject: URGENT: Special Maintenance Rule for Concrete Mixers

Hi Team,

Regardless of what the current SRS (v1.2) says about the dynamic Maintenance Matrix, we have an emergency with Concrete Mixers. 120 minutes is absolutely not enough for proper cleaning/maintenance.

Effective immediately:
- Concrete Mixers MUST have a 12-hour (720 min) maintenance window.
- All other machinery can stay at the 2-hour (120 min) rule for now.

Please hardcode this for the Mixer category until the official Matrix is published in the next SRS version.

Best regards,
Tom (Operations Lead)

Hi Dev Team,

Support keeps running into cases where a high-priority customer wants to secure an item even though the system currently treats the time window as blocked because of another pending request.

Operationally, the team is asking whether specially authorized staff should be able to intervene in those cases and resolve the conflict manually, rather than forcing the customer to wait for the ordinary availability flow to clear on its own. In practice this would mean allowing a priority booking path to take precedence over weaker, not-yet-confirmed demand.

Please do not treat this as confirmed product policy yet. We need guidance on whether this should remain a support-side exception process, or whether the booking logic itself is expected to support it.
